previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, hypertension, GERD, recurrent DVT/PE on warfarin, and chronic constipation presented with left lower quadrant abdominal pain, constipation, vomiting, and decreased urine output. She was found to have hyponatremia and hypokalemia likely due to poor oral intake and vomiting. A CT scan showed extensive diverticulosis without diverticulitis or acute obstruction. She was treated with IV fluids, potassium repletion, and a senna enema, which led to a bowel movement and significant pain relief. She subsequently developed transient diarrhea, which resolved without infection on stool studies. Her iron supplements were held due to contribution to constipation, and her warfarin dose was maintained with plans for Coumadin clinic follow-up. She improved clinically, maintained stable electrolytes, and was discharged home with instructions to avoid iron, use simethicone for bloating, and follow up with her primary care physician.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___ 

COMPARISON:  Prior exam from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ female with generalized weakness, question
pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  AP upright and lateral views of the chest were provided.  The heart
remains mildly enlarged.  There is mild pulmonary interstitial edema without
pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  No convincing signs of pneumonia. 
Mediastinal contour is stable.  Bony structures appear intact with chronic
degenerative changes at the shoulders bilaterally.

IMPRESSION:  Mild cardiomegaly with mild pulmonary interstitial edema.

HISTORY:  Elevated INR with generalized weakness. 

TECHNIQUE:  Contigous axial images were obtained through the brain without
intravenous contrast.  Multiplanar reformatted images were prepared and
reviewed.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior head CTs with the most recent from ___.  

FINDINGS: There is no evidence of an acute intracranial hemorrhage, edema,
large vessel territorial infarction, or shift of the midline structures.  The
ventricles and sulci are prominent in size and configuration, consistent with
age-related cortical atrophy.  Bilateral periventricular white matter
hypodensities are again noted is typical of chronic small vessel ischemic
changes.  More confluent hypodensities are again noted bilateral basal ganglia
suggestive of prior lacunar infarctions.  No acute fractures are identified. 
The visualized mastoid air cells and paranasal sinuses are clear. 

IMPRESSION: No acute intracranial injury.

HISTORY:  Hematocrit drop, elevated INR, assess for retroperitoneal bleed.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial helical MDCT of the abdomen and pelvis was performed without
IV and oral contrast.  Multiplanar sagittal and coronal reformatted images
were generated.  DLP:  913.49 mGy-cm.  

COMPARISON:  This study is compared to previous CT abdomen and pelvis from
___.

FINDINGS:  

CT ABDOMEN:  
The assessment of the intra-abdominal organs is limited without intravenous or
oral contrast.

There are increased atelectatic changes at the lung bases, right worse than
left, and atelectasis is also noted in the lingula.

The liver, gallbladder, adrenal glands, kidneys, and spleen appear
unremarkable.  The pancreas is atrophic.  There is mild atherosclerosis of the
abdominal aorta and iliac arteries, without aneurysmal dilatation; assessment
of the vasculature is limited on this non-contrast study.  There are no
findings to suggest retroperitoneal hemorrhage.

There is extensive colonic diverticulosis without diverticulitis.  The small
bowel appears unremarkable.  There is no retroperitoneal or intra-abdominal
lymphadenopathy.  There is no ascites.

CT PELVIS:  
Assessment of the pelvis is limited by artifact from left hip arthroplasty. 
There is no pelvic or retroperitoneal hemorrhage.  There is a Foley catheter
within the bladder with gas pockets in the bladder likely secondary to
catheterization.  The uterus appears unremarkable.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  
There are moderate-to-severe degenerative changes of the lower lumbar spine,
overall similar to previous.  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic bone lesions
are identified.  There has been previous left hip arthroplasty.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No signs suggestive of retroperitoneal hemorrhage.
2.  Bibasilar atelectatic changes, right side worse than left.

HISTORY:  Left-sided PICC line placement.

TECHNIQUE:  Single, AP, portable chest radiograph was obtained with patient in
an upright position.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to radiographs dated ___.

FINDINGS:

There has been interval placement of a left-sided PICC line with the tip seen
extending into the right atrium, 3-4 cm below the cavoatrial junction.  As
compared to the prior examination, there has been little interval change. 
Redemonstrated is mild pulmonary edema, mild cardiomegaly, and several right
upper lobe nodules seen better on prior chest CT examination.  There is no
overt pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or focal consolidation identified.  The
mediastinal contours are stable.

IMPRESSION:

Interval placement of a left-sided PICC line with the tip seen extending into
the right atrium, 3-4 cm below the cavoatrial junction.
